subject: AWS private offer: term slicing options, CFO escrow & buyer approval path
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@catalystlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@catalystlabs.com>
Cc: procurement@catalystlabs.com
Date: Fri, 1 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer — term structure & CFO questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Catalyst Labs is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. We are trying to map how a private offer would land in our procurement flow. Two things came up on our side: 1) Our CFO is pushing for an escrow-style protection for any pre-paid committed spend for pilots that roll into annual commitments; 2) Procurement needs clarity on buyer approvals for AWS private offers across our finance vs. business units.

Questions:
- Are you able to split a private offer into a short pilot (3 months) followed by an annual commit (9 months) under a single private-offer activation?
- What evidence can you provide for finance (SOC 2 report, data retention / access controls)?
- If we need to require CFO signoff or an escrow clause, how does Redwood typically handle proration/refunds mid-term?

We can share a PO stub if that helps. Would like to move quickly — can you folks jump on a 30m call next week?

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Director, Product & Partnerships
Catalyst Labs

--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@catalystlabs.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@catalystlabs.com>, procurement@catalystlabs.com
Date: Fri, 1 Sep 2028 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — term structure & CFO questions

Hi Elena — great to hear from you, and glad the demo resonated. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a split pilot + commit in a single private-offer activation; yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and the data-retention statement; and yes, finance/proration is manageable — we typically handle mid-term terminations with pro-rated refunds per the seller terms or apply remaining credit to future invoices depending on the agreed flow.

Details:
- Term slicing: we can structure the private offer as a single contract with two billing tranches: a 3-month pilot at a reduced usage tier, then auto-transition to a 9-month annual commitment with a pre-agreed unit price. Activation is handled via the AWS Private Offer acceptance flow and the buyer's Marketplace admin will see the offer as one activation with staged billing rules.
- CFO / escrow: we don't maintain customer-managed escrow accounts by default. Typical options are: (A) Redwood issues pro-rated refunds on termination; (B) Redwood accepts a restricted escrow arrangement for larger commitments (requires legal & finance approval — we can scope this as a non-standard term); (C) we can include a holdback on payment tied to phased acceptance.
- Evidence: attaching SOC2 summary and a short pricing_breakdown.xlsx for the two-tranche proposal, plus our standard redwood_po_template_v2.pdf for procurement review.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review attached pricing_breakdown.xlsx and redwood_po_template_v2.pdf.
2) Ben Carter (cc'd) will weigh in on proration mechanics and any finance gating.
3) If you still prefer escrow, I will loop Legal and provide a draft SOW + escrow approach options.

Available times for a 30m call: Mon 9/4 10:00-12:00 PT or Tue 9/5 14:00-16:00 PT. Which works for you?

Best,
Soogin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: pricing_breakdown.xlsx (Excel, 12KB); redwood_po_template_v2.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Adding a quick ops note from marketplace side.

On Fri, Sep 1, 2028 at 1:30 PM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena — great to hear from you, and glad the demo resonated. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a split pilot + commit in a single private-offer activation; yes, we can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and the data-retention statement; and yes, finance/proration is manageable — we typically handle mid-term terminations with pro-rated refunds per the seller terms or apply remaining credit to future invoices depending on the agreed flow.

Marketplace specifics:
- AWS buyer approval: for standard private offers the buyer's AWS Marketplace admin accepts the offer — if the buyer requires internal CFO approval, that is outside Marketplace flow and needs to be coordinated as part of the customer's legal signoff.
- Timing: expect 2-5 business days to get the private-offer activated on the buyer side once the offer is submitted from our Seller Central and the buyer accepts. For escrow/non-standard payment terms, plan for an additional 7-10 business days for legal review.
- Billing handoff: once activated, AWS invoices per our private-offer settings and we reconcile. For any special holds/escrow, finance will need a routing instruction which Ben can provide.

I'll be on the 9/4 call to help with Marketplace flows.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi all — Ben from RevOps here, quick finance mechanics so procurement can validate internally.

On Sat, Sep 2, 2028 at 10:05 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marketplace specifics:
> - AWS buyer approval: for standard private offers the buyer's AWS Marketplace admin accepts the offer — if the buyer requires internal CFO approval, that is outside Marketplace flow and needs to be coordinated as part of the customer's legal signoff.

Proration rules (examples attached in proration_examples.pdf):
- If Catalyst signs a 12-month combined arrangement (3m pilot + 9m commit) for $120,000 total and terminates after month 4: we calculate used value for months billed, then refund the remaining unused prepaid portion less any agreed early-termination fee. Example: 4 months used = $40,000 consumed; remaining $80,000 prorated less 10% termination fee = refund $72,000.
- If you prefer to avoid refunds, we can structure the pilot as a consumption invoice (no prepay) and only prepay the annual commit when it transitions — this reduces escrow needs but does change unit economics.

Escrow / holdback: we can accept a buyer request for funds to be held in escrow, but that requires: (1) written request from buyer procurement; (2) legal-approved escrow language; (3) a payment route (third-party escrow provider or custodian). This typically adds 7-14 business days.

DocuSign & HubSpot: once terms are agreed we will send DocuSign from Redwood Legal. HubSpot deal id: 1234567 (see link below).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
